name: Kolkata Police
license_or_status: public domain as stated on Wikimedia Commons (PD-textlogo, insignia; the Lion Capital PD-India); trademark/insignia of Kolkata Police
notes: Blue star badge with 'KOLKATA POLICE FORCE' round the national emblem, from the force's heraldry page (kolkatapolice.gov.in/heraldry). Also stands for Kolkata Traffic Police, which uses the same badge in gold. Dark blue artwork on transparent: needs a light plate on dark grounds. Contains the State Emblem of India, whose use is restricted by the State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use) Act, 2005

name: West Bengal Police
license_or_status: non-free logo (en.wikipedia; file page licence: Fair use)
notes: Red and navy shield with the national emblem, laurel, 'WBP' monogram and 'WEST BENGAL POLICE' (vector). The navy half would merge into a near-black ground, so it gets a light plate. Contains the State Emblem of India, whose use is restricted by the State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use) Act, 2005

name: Bidhannagar Police Commissionerate
license_or_status: non-free logo (en.wikipedia; file page licence: Fair use; tagged non-free seal)
notes: Silver-edged blue shield reading 'BIDHANNAGAR CITY POLICE' over a 'COURAGE CARE COMMITMENT' ribbon; the file page cites bidhannagarcitypolice.com. Only 180x179 at source. Contains the State Emblem of India, whose use is restricted by the State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use) Act, 2005

name: Howrah City Police
license_or_status: non-free logo (en.wikipedia; file page licence: Fair use)
notes: Grey-edged blue shield reading 'HOWRAH CITY POLICE' over a 'COURAGE CARE COMMITMENT' ribbon; the file page cites howrahcitypolice.in. Only 140x156 at source. Contains the State Emblem of India, whose use is restricted by the State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use) Act, 2005

name: Kolkata Municipal Corporation
license_or_status: public domain as stated on Wikimedia Commons (PD-India); emblem of Kolkata Municipal Corporation
notes: The corporation's emblem (adopted 1961, from kmcgov.in): a hand of fire in the centre, 'Purosree Bibardhan' and 'Kolkata Paurosangstha' in Bengali, rice stalks, fish and a Mayurpankhi boat, with a lotus, a wheel, a svastika (for prosperity, as the corporation describes it) and a double thunderbolt in the corners. Yellow on navy, reads on any ground

name: New Town Kolkata Development Authority
license_or_status: official website logo file (nkdamar.org); no licence stated
notes: Stacked 'NKDA' letters in blues and brown with the full name across the middle. Not on Commons or en.wikipedia. The source is an opaque 1430x1680 image whose white gaps between the letters run to the edges, so the white is part of the mark and was kept (no background removal); it reads as a solid tile on any ground

name: Disaster Management & Civil Defence Department, Government of West Bengal
license_or_status: official website logo file (wbdmd.gov.in); no licence stated; fetched from the Internet Archive copy because the live site refused connections
notes: Gold seal reading 'GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL' and 'WBDMD' round the national emblem: the mark of the state Disaster Management & Civil Defence Department, used because the West Bengal State Disaster Management Authority has no mark of its own on file. The department's site header shows the same seal as images/logo2.png (95x95, still captured in 2024); the 937x938 master was used. A near-invisible soft glow at the bottom edge was trimmed off with the margin. Contains the State Emblem of India, whose use is restricted by the State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use) Act, 2005

name: National Disaster Management Authority
license_or_status: non-free logo (en.wikipedia; file page licence: Fair use)
notes: Circular NDMA seal with the map of India inside a gold cog ring; reads on any ground

name: NDMA Sachet (National Disaster Alert Portal)
license_or_status: official website logo file (sachet.ndma.gov.in); no licence stated
notes: White 'Sachet / National Disaster Alert Portal' wordmark from the portal header. Not on Commons or en.wikipedia. White artwork: needs a dark plate on light grounds

name: India Meteorological Department
license_or_status: non-free logo (en.wikipedia; file page licence: Fair use)
notes: IMD seal (globe with weather map) with the national emblem on top. The dark emblem fades on a near-black ground, so it gets a light plate. Contains the State Emblem of India, whose use is restricted by the State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use) Act, 2005

name: Metro Railway, Kolkata
license_or_status: public domain as stated on Wikimedia Commons (PD-textlogo) + trademarked; trademark of Metro Railway, Kolkata
notes: Red stylised 'M' of two slanted blocks (vector), the mark used by Metro Railway, Kolkata (the logo on its en.wikipedia article). Reads on dark and light grounds

name: West Bengal Transport Corporation
license_or_status: official website logo file (wbtconline.in); no licence stated
notes: Round blue seal reading 'WEST BENGAL TRANSPORT CORPORATION' and its Bengali name, with the Biswa Bangla mark of the Government of West Bengal in the centre. LOW RESOLUTION: only 100x100 at source (kept at native size). The only WBTC-related file on Commons is an uploader-made 'temporary' text banner, which was not used

name: OpenStreetMap
license_or_status: CC BY-SA 3.0 + trademarked (Wikimedia Commons); trademark of the OpenStreetMap Foundation
notes: Magnifying glass over a folded map (vector). OSM map data itself is ODbL and needs its own credit

name: Open-Meteo
license_or_status: official website icon file (open-meteo.com; the site's source repository open-meteo/open-meteo-website is AGPL-3.0); no separate logo licence stated
notes: Orange rounded square with 'om', the site's own app icon (512x512 at source). Not on Commons or en.wikipedia. The GitHub organisation avatar was not used because it sets the mark on a photo

name: Copernicus

name: Cesium
license_or_status: official website logo file (cesium.com; a trademark of Cesium GS, Inc.); no licence stated
notes: Cesium logomark (vector) on its own white disc, so it reads on any ground
